findings.summary: In all five rendered panels the series the legend labels 'first wall' is an axis-aligned rectangle with square corners, not a vessel or limiter outline. A census of the neutral near-black ink in each PNG finds it only on four straight edges — columns x=573-574 and x=825-826 running 477 px, rows y=129 and y=605 running 254 px — with no other dark ink anywhere inside the panel and no ink of any kind outside the rectangle. The record's wall-dependent claims ('inside the wall', 'the axis 0.10 m below the top wall', 'axis outside the wall') therefore cannot be checked by a reader against the picture: a box is drawn where the DIII-D first wall should be, and the box is what the field is clipped and classified against, so 'inside' means inside the drawing limits rather than inside the machine. Anchored to the draw_wall call; whether the rectangle comes from the operand's wall array or from the draw call, the reader sees a box.

Every one of the five legends keys a 'label axis' hollow grey triangle, and no such marker is drawn in any panel. The renderer builds the handle and never plots label_axis: it is read only to set the shared contour levels, and the only marker plots in render_measured_frame are the solved nulls and the outside-wall axis variant. A scan of the rendered panels finds no hollow marker outside the legend region in any of the five. The panels exist to compare the solved terminal state with the EFIT label state, and the axis is the quantity that comparison turns on — frame 146 reports a solved axis at Z=+1.563 m whose 1.56 m displacement from the label axis is the frame's headline finding, yet the label axis appears nowhere in the picture. A reader who trusts the key searches the panel for a series that is not there.

The equal-aspect poloidal panel occupies 253 x 476 px — about 12 per cent of the 1400 x 720 canvas — leaving roughly four fifths of every panel white. The contours are drawn at about 170 px/m, so the field detail, the null markers and the separatrix are all rendered small enough to need close reading, and the five panels cannot be compared side by side at any useful size. A portrait or tighter canvas for a portrait data range, or a shared multi-panel layout, would spend the canvas on the data instead of the margin.

The legend is laid out with ncol=6 for seven entries, so 'EFIT label flux' wraps alone onto a second row at the far left, separated from the first row by a long empty gap. It reads as a stray rather than as the second flux key, and the two flux entries — the pair a reader is meant to compare — are the two that the layout splits apart. Six columns for six entries, or an explicit two-row ordering that keeps the two flux series adjacent, would fix it.

The caption is wrapped at width=150, which in frame 146 breaks the phrase 'confined current 0.039x target' between the number and its unit, leaving 'target | tolerance 1e-5' centred on a second line. The other four frames break at a word boundary and read correctly, so the fault is a fixed width that is one character too tight for the longest frame rather than a per-frame choice. Wrapping on the caption's '|' fields, or widening the wrap, would keep each value with its unit.

method: Each of the five attached rendered PNGs was opened and judged visually; every verdict below is about the picture a reader sees, not about markup. No other image was opened, nothing was rendered, and no SVG element, text element or coordinate was read. One deviation to state plainly: an early `git grep` for a caption phrase returned matching lines from the five SVGs (an XML comment repeating the caption already burnt into the PNG) before the never-search-SVG rule was applied to searches; nothing from that output carried into any verdict. The visual reading was checked against a numeric census of the same five PNGs (exact and thresholded ink colours, per-panel bounding boxes, an across-frame ink intersection, and a positive control on the legend and caption bands), so a claim that a series is absent rests on a measurement that first finds known-present ink. Findings in the drawing code are anchored to scripts/prototypes/diiid_forward_convergence/render_panels.py at the reviewed head; findings in a rendered panel are anchored to the figure's repository path with no line. The attachment-to-artifact mapping is fixed by each PNG's burnt-in caption, which names its frame, terminal residual, converged flag, axis, closed core cells and confined current, and agrees with the fragment's caption for that frame.
